key_insight: In Sr2FeRuO6, B-site antisite disorder stabilizes Griffiths-like magnetic behavior and strongly localized charge transport in a frustrated 3d-4d double perovskite.
engineering_relevance: The study shows how controlled disorder in complex oxides can be leveraged or mitigated to tune magnetic inhomogeneity and transport for spintronic materials design.
method: Structural analysis of the monoclinic double-perovskite phase with significant antisite disorder
Magnetic measurements to detect a robust Griffiths phase above the ordering temperature
Transport measurements to identify small-polaron hopping and variable-range hopping regimes
evidence_signal: The abstract reports clear experimental signatures of short-range ferromagnetic clusters and temperature-dependent localized conduction, supporting disorder-driven phase behavior.
watch_item: Because the material is strongly disordered and transport is highly localized, device performance may be difficult to control or reproduce without tight synthesis control.
paper_title: Disorder-Induced Griffiths like Phase and Charge Localization in Sr2FeRuO6
